Descriptions are made by individuals who may not have expertise specific to this type of item, in consultation with local and Internet resources. Shoppers are cautioned to evaluate items based upon their own resources. No guarantee of authenticity is implied unless specifically stated.
How Photography Affects Size Perception
Macro (extreme close-up) photography is heavily utilized in jewelry listings, enabling viewers to examine pieces in larger-than-life detail. An accurate understanding of the actual sizes of these pieces cannot be deduced using photos alone. It is important that the bidder takes close note of the measurements and weights to determine actual sizes.
About Gemstone & Metal Testing
Gemstones are tested with a Presidium Gem Tester. Goodwill of the Olympics & Rainier Region is a member of the International Gem Society; however, as we are not certified gemologists, we cannot guarantee the authenticity of any gemstone unless otherwise stated. Gemstone identification information is provided for your reference and consideration in bidding; no guarantee is implied.
Pearls are tested with a check for grittiness to detect nacre irregularities. We are generally unable to specify pearl types and characteristics; they may be cultured, wild, freshwater or saltwater pearls. Coral may be natural or dyed; most of our coral listings include dyed pieces.
Metals including Gold, Silver, and Platinum are tested using an XRF precious metal analyzer, the Niton XL2 by Thermo Scientific, unless explicitly noted otherwise. XRF (X-ray fluorescence) analysis is a non-destructive testing method able to determine an item's elemental composition. Identification of other non-magnetic metals, including brass, bronze, copper, tin, and titanium, rely on our best estimation, and no guarantee is implied; they have not been tested or positively identified unless explicitly noted otherwise. Some jewelry may contain non-precious metals in clasps or findings, causing parts of the piece to respond to a magnet.
